background.summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: asymptotic analysis, algorithm design basics (divide and conquer, recurrences, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication), discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, induction, permutations), and linear algebra and calculus at the usual first-course level. They know polynomials, complex numbers with roots of unity, and simple Turing machines with tapes. They have not studied the FFT in depth, Fourier analysis on groups, tensor products, numerical analysis, or fast integer multiplication research.
